contents.name: Definition (1.1) and §2.3: Kronecker coefficients g(lambda,mu,nu), their S_3 and conjugation symmetries (2.3), and the three-character formula
§2.3 symmetry (2.3): g(lambda,mu,nu) = g(lambda',mu',nu) = g(lambda,mu',nu') and full S_3 symmetry
Theorem 1.1 (k-stability): G_k(t) = g(lambda + (t^k), mu + (t^k), nu + (tk)) is bounded and monotone increasing, hence eventually constant
§4.1 Theorem 4.1: conditional preservation under condition (*), min{lambda_k,mu_k} >= max{lambda_{k+1},mu_{k+1}} + (n - nu_1), for all t >= 0
§4.1 Corollary 4.2 [PP3 Cor. 8.3]: the k = 1 case, g(lambda,mu,nu) = g(lambda+(t),mu+(t),nu+(t)) under lambda_1 + nu_1 <= n + max{lambda_2,mu_2}
§4.2 Lemma 4.3 (Reduction Lemma) stated with the reduction map phi and the bound r <= 2 s l^2
§4.2 Example 4.4: lambda = mu = (2,2), nu = (3,1), g(lambda,mu,nu) = 0 while g((2+t,2),(2+t,2),(3+t,1)) = 1 for all t >= 1
Theorem 2.2 (Manivel's inequality: g(lambda+alpha,mu+beta,nu+gamma) >= max(g(lambda,mu,nu), g(alpha,beta,gamma)) for positive partners)
contents.reason: Manivel's inequality is proved by a geometric no-zero-divisor argument on the algebra of GL(V)xGL(W)-covariants (Manivel 2015), outside this pair's representation-theoretic proof scope; the page claims only the eventual-constancy consequence of k-stability and asserts no monotonicity, exactly as the design directs.

sources.title: Igor Pak and Greta Panova, On the complexity of computing Kronecker coefficients, arXiv:1404.0653v3 (2015)
sources.locator: §2.2-2.3 pp. 3-4 (Kronecker coefficients, symmetric-function conventions, Littlewood's identity (1), generalized Cauchy identity (2)); §5.1 pp. 8-12 (the Reduction Lemma 5.1 with its complete proof: equation (3), part (i) and part (ii), the reduction map phi and the Jacobi-Trudi expansion (7)); §8.9 pp. 17-18 (reduced Kronecker coefficients and Corollary 8.3). Owner reconciliation uses the corrected PP3 reduction display with sentinel l+1 and ind_I block rank; the older Bounds display is not used for the map.

contents.name: §5.1 Lemma 5.1 (Reduction Lemma) with the complete proof of parts (i) and (ii), including the reduction map phi, equation (3) and the Jacobi-Trudi expansion (7)
§2.3 Littlewood's identity (1): s_lambda * (s_tau s_theta) = sum c^lambda_{alpha,beta} (s_alpha * s_tau)(s_beta * s_theta)
§8.9 Corollary 8.3 and its proof sketch: the reduction map makes the padded sequence independent of n beyond an explicit bound
§2.4 Theorem 2.1 (the semigroup property of Kronecker coefficients, proved in [CHM] with the geometric method)
contents.reason: The semigroup property is the positivity part of the geometric theory of the Kronecker cone (Christandl-Harrow-Mitchison); the pair needs only the explicit reduction lemma and k-stability, and importing the geometric proof would exceed this page.

contents.name: §§3-4, 6-7 (complexity of Kron, hook partitions, Blasiak's interpretation, characters of S_n)
contents.reason: These are complexity-theoretic and hook-specific applications of the reduction technique; no claim of this pair depends on them and the page makes no complexity assertion.

contents.name: Definition 3.2.1 and Proposition 3.4.1: the padded family V(lambda)_n = V_{lambda[n]} begins at n >= |lambda| + lambda_1, so the padding threshold is exact

contents.reason: The FI-module proof of eventual constancy of g_n(alpha,beta,gamma) belongs to the later Murnaghan-stability pair, which is planned and scaffolded in this run; this pair only records the padded notation without asserting constancy.

contents.name: Theorem 3.3.4 and the character-polynomial construction for finitely generated FI-modules
contents.reason: Character polynomials and representation stability are the subject of the separately planned SYMR-14 pair; they are not used by the internal-product and Kronecker-coefficient claims of this batch.

contents.name: The padded partition notation alpha[n] = (n - |alpha|, alpha_1, alpha_2, ...) and its domain n >= |alpha| + alpha_1 (p. 3)

contents.reason: The exact threshold theorem and the reduced-coefficient expansion are proved on the planned Murnaghan-stability pair, which consumes only the padded-sequence notation registered here.

contents.name: Lemma 2.1 (nonnegative expansion of a reduced Kronecker coefficient into ordinary Kronecker and LR coefficients)
contents.reason: The expansion and its degree-matching consequences are the supply for the reduced-coefficient support and threshold theorems, all of which belong to the later Murnaghan-stability pair.
